newsitem.title: ITALY: Cambodian arrested in Rome in suspected child ring.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian arrested in Rome in suspected child ring.

text.p: A Cambodian man was being questioned on Sunday on suspicion of involvement in a child smuggling ring after he was arrested at Rome airport with fake Belgian papers and four children who were not his, police said.
Cao Leng Huot, 51, was carrying photographs of hundreds of children and an address book containing many addresses and telephone numbers when he was arrested at Fiumicino airport on Saturday.
The Cambodian, speaking fluent French, told police the two boys and two girls with him, aged between about six and 12, were his own children. They flew into Rome from Phnom Penh via Hong Kong.
He said other children in hundreds of photographs found in his luggage were relatives.
"I always carry their pictures with me," Corriere della Sera newspaper reported him as saying.
But one of the children, who also carried false Belgian identity papers and had no luggage, shouted out that he was lying and that the Cambodian was not their father.
Airport officials became suspicious after finding the passport he was carrying was on a blacklist of stolen documents.
Huot was held overnight in jail and was being questioned by magistrates on Sunday. The children were in care in Rome.
Newspapers said investigations were still at an early stage but the case raised images of a child abduction, sex and murder scandal that has shaken Belgium for three months.
